api_token.description: Elestio API token. You can find this token in the [security settings](https://dash.elest.io/account/security) of your account.

email.description: Elestio email address. This is the email address with which you registered on the [Elestio website](https://dash.elest.io/).

admin_email.description: Service admin email. Requires replace to change it.

app_auto_updates_day_of_week.description: Service app auto update day of week. `0 = Sunday`, `1 = Monday`, ..., `6 = Saturday`, `-1 = Everyday`

backups_enabled.description: Service backups state.  Requires a support_level higher than `level1`. **Default** `false`.

custom_domain_names.description: Indicate the list of domains for which you want to activate HTTPS / TLS / SSL. You will also need to create a DNS entry on your domain name (from your registrar control panel) pointing to your service. You must create a CNAME record pointing to the service `cname` value. Alternatively, you can create an A record pointing to the service `ipv4` value.

datacenter.description: The datacenter of the provider where the service will be hosted. You can look for available datacenters in the [providers documentation](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elestio/elestio/latest/docs/guides/providers_datacenters_server_types). Requires replace to change it.

default_password.description: Set the default password used by you services at **CREATION** time.</br>The password can only contain alphanumeric characters or hyphens `-`. Require at least 10 characters, one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter and one number.</br>If you don't set a password, a random one will be generated by the API.</br>This attribute will **not be synced** after the creation. Use `admin.password` or `database_admin.password` to get the current password after the creation.

elestio_id.description: Service identifier unique and handled by Elestio.

external_backups_retain_day_of_week.description: Service external backups retain day of week. `0 = Sunday`, `1 = Monday`, ..., `6 = Saturday`, `-1 = Everyday`

external_backups_update_day_of_week.description: Service external backups update day. `0 = Sunday`, `1 = Monday`, ..., `6 = Saturday`, `-1 = Everyday`

firewall_remove_tool_ports.description: When `true`, removes API-managed tool ports (VS Code, Terminal, etc.) that are not explicitly defined in `firewall_user_rules`. Tool ports explicitly included in `firewall_user_rules` are user-managed and will always be preserved. **Default** `false`. Use temporarily for cleanup, then reset to `false`.

targets.description: CIDR blocks allowed to access this port.

type.description: The firewall rule type.

firewall_tool_rules.description: API-managed tool ports (VS Code, Terminal, File Explorer, etc.) that are not explicitly defined in `firewall_user_rules`. These ports are automatically managed by the API and will be preserved unless `firewall_remove_tool_ports` is set to `true`. If you want to manage a tool port yourself, include it explicitly in `firewall_user_rules`.

targets.description: CIDR blocks allowed to access this port. Use `["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"]` to allow access from all IPv4/IPv6 addresses. **Note:** Required system ports (22/tcp/input, 4242/udp/input, and 80/tcp/input when using custom domains) must have exactly these two targets and cannot have additional target restrictions.

type.description: The firewall rule type. Currently only `input` is supported.

firewall_user_rules.description: Firewall rules for the service. **Required ports (must use exactly `["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"]`):** `22/tcp` (SSH), `4242/udp` (Nebula VPN), `80/tcp` (Let's Encrypt for custom domains). When `firewall_enabled` is `false`, set to `[]`. **Software default ports:** `80/tcp`, `443/tcp`.

id.description: Service identifier handled by the provider. The format can change.

keep_backups_on_delete_enabled.description: Creates a backup and keeps all existing ones after deleting the service. If the project is deleted, the backups will be lost. **Default** `true`.

local_field.description: This field is dynamic and can be used to store any custom data that you want to retrieve later in your configuration. It is not used by the provider.

local_field_sensitive.description: Same as `local_field` but the value is sensitive.

project_id.description: Identifier of the project in which the service is. Requires replace to change it.

provider_name.description: The name of the provider to use to host the service (must be lowercase). Common providers: `hetzner`, `do`, `lightsail`, `linode`, `vultr`, `scaleway`, `netcup`. You can look for available provider names in the [providers documentation](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elestio/elestio/latest/docs/guides/providers_datacenters_server_types). Requires replace to change it.

server_name.description: Service server name. Max length 60 characters, and can only include lowercase letters a-z, digits 0-9, and hyphens (-). Must be unique within the project. Requires replace to change it.

server_type.description:
The server type defines the power and memory allocated to the service. Each `provider_name` has a list of available server types. You can look for available server types in the [providers documentation](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elestio/elestio/latest/docs/guides/providers_datacenters_server_types). You can only upgrade it, not downgrade.
Requires replace to update the server type with the provider `scale_way`.

public_key.description: SSH Public Key.The SSH public key should only contain two parts separated by a space. Example: `ssh-rsa AAaCfa...WAqDUNs=`. You should not include the username, hostname, or comment.

ssh_keys.description: This attribute allows you to add SSH keys to your service.

key_data.description: The Public Key value without comment. Use `provider::elestio::parse_ssh_key_data(file("~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub"))` to remove the comment from your key. Read the guide ["How to use SSH keys with Elestio Terraform Provider"](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elestio/elestio/latest/docs/guides/ssh_keys).

username.description: The username is used to identify the Public Key among others. Must be unique (per resource).

ssh_public_keys.description: You can add Public Keys to your resource to access it via the SSH protocol.

support_level.description: Service support level. Available support levels are `level1`, `level2` and `level3`. You can look for their advantages in the [pricing documentation](https://elest.io/pricing). Requires replace the whole resource to change it in terraform. It is recommended to use the web dashboard to change it without replacing the service.

system_auto_updates_reboot_day_of_week.description: Service system auto update reboot day of week. `0 = Sunday`, `1 = Monday`, ..., `6 = Saturday`, `-1 = Everyday`

system_auto_updates_reboot_hour.description: Service system auto update reboot hour.

system_auto_updates_reboot_minute.description: Service system auto update reboot minute.

system_auto_updates_security_patches_onl.description: Service system auto update security patches only state. **Default** `false`.

template_id.description: The template identifier defines the software used. You can look for available template ids in the [templates documentation](https://elest.io/fully-managed-services).

version.description: This is the version of the software used as service. **Default** `latest`.

targets.description: CIDR blocks allowed to access this port.

parse_ssh_key.description: Takes an SSH public key and a username parameter. Returns an object with `key_data` (the key without comment) and `username` (from the provided value or extracted from the key comment). The username parameter is required but accepts null - pass null explicitly to extract the username from the SSH key comment. If username is null and the key has no comment, an error is returned.
parse_ssh_key.summary: Parses an SSH public key and extracts key data and username

parameters.name: ssh_key
parameters.description: The SSH public key string (e.g., 'ssh-rsa AAAA... user@host')

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The username to use. Pass null explicitly to extract the username from the SSH key comment.

parse_ssh_key_data.description: Takes an SSH public key string and returns only the key type and key data, removing any trailing comment. This is useful because Elestio does not accept SSH keys with comments.
parse_ssh_key_data.summary: Strips the comment from an SSH public key

parameters.name: ssh_key
parameters.description: The SSH public key string (e.g., 'ssh-rsa AAAA... user@host')
